population.description: Adults performing aerobic/endurance exercise, at low-to-moderate doses (1.3-3 mg/kg)

gradeRationale.note: Dose-response relationship is well established at low-to-moderate doses; doses above 6 mg/kg are understudied with an unclear risk-benefit profile and are deliberately excluded from what this claim supports.

statement: Low-to-moderate doses of caffeine (roughly 1.3-3 mg/kg) reliably improve aerobic time-trial exercise performance; higher doses are not well studied and are not supported by this evidence.

citations.title: Dose-Response Effect of Oral Caffeine Use on Aerobic Exercise Performance: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

review.note: Drafted from master research list v2 (2026-09-05). Stimulant with known caution areas (cardiac arrhythmia, anxiety disorders, pregnancy) - see safety-caffeine-cardiac-anxiety.json draft and the existing global pregnancy rule.
